name: Graded Pragmatic Belief Allocation with Synonyms
summary: Listeners distribute 10 confidence points across candidate referents in scenes with synonymous labels and prior queries.

charter.question: How do listeners allocate graded belief across candidate referents when multiple words can apply to the same feature extension?

instructions.welcome: Welcome! In this study you will look at groups of friendly robots and judge how likely each robot is to be the one a speaker means.
instructions.task: On each screen you will see several robots. A speaker who sees the exact same robots says a single word that describes a part of the robot they mean (or on some screens, you will judge which robot they are most likely to talk about before hearing any word). You have 10 points to split across the robots: put more points on robots you think are more likely, and 0 points on any robot that does not have the named part. If only one robot has that part, put all 10 points on that robot. Your points on each screen must add up to 10.

comprehension_checks.question: How do you answer on each screen?
options: Split all 10 points across the robots based on how likely each robot is to be the one the speaker means.
Give 10 points to every robot on the screen.
Type a description of the robots.

comprehension_checks.question: How many points should you give to a robot that does NOT have the part the speaker named?
options: 0 points, because the speaker's word is always true of the robot they mean.
